sentences.text: Uncle Remus and Brer Rabbit by Joel Chandler Harris.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: The Creatures Go to the Barbecue.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: "Once pon a time," said Uncle Remus to the little boy, 'But when was once upon a time?' the child interrupted to ask.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: The old man smiled.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: 'I spec' 'twas one time or two times, and maybe a time and a half.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: You know when Johnny Ashcake gone to bake?
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Well, 'twas long in dem days.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Once upon a time,' he resumed, 'Mistah Man had a garden so fine dat all de neighbors come to see it.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Some would look at it over de fence, —some would peek through de cracks, and some would come and look at it by de light of de stars.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: And one of 'em was ole Brer Rabbit.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Starlight, moonlight, cloudlight, de night-light was de light for him.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: When de turn of de mornin' come, he is always up and about a-feelin' pretty well, I thank you, sah.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Now den you done hear what I say.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Dere was Mr. Man, Yonder was de garden, en hier was ole Brer Rabbit.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Uncle Remus made a map of this part of the story by marking in the sand with his walking cane.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: "Well, dis bein' de case, what you spec' gwine ter happen?" "Nuthin' in de round world but what ben happenin' sence greens en sparragrass was planted in de ground.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Dey look fine, en dey taste fine; en long towards de shank er de mawnin' Brer Rabbit would creep through de crack in de fence and nibble at 'em.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: He'd take de greens but leave his tracks, mo' specially right atter a rain.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Takin' and leavin' is de way o' de world.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Well, one mornin', Mr. Man went out in his truck patch, and he finds something missing—a cabbage here, a turnip dar, and a mess of beans yonder.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: And he asks, 'How come dis?' He look round, he did, and he seed Brer Rabbit's tracks what he couldn't take wid him.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Brer Rabbit had left his shoes at home and come barfooted.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: So Mr. Man he call his dogs— 'Here, Buck!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Here, Bringer!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Here, Blue!'—and he sic 'em on de track, and heah dey went!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Whew!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: You'd a-thunk dey was runnin' after 40 limb rhinoceroses, from de fuss dey made!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Brer Rabbit he hear 'em coming, and he put out for home, kinder doubling round like he do dese days.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: When he got to de p'int wher' he kin sit down for to rest his face in his hands, he tuck a poplar leaf and he gone to fan hisself.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Den Brer Fox come a-troddin' up.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: He say: "Brer Rabbit, what's all dis fuss I hear in de woods?
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: What de name o' goodness do it mean?" Brer Rabbit kinder scratched his head and lowed: "Why, dey ain't trying for to drive me to de big barbecue on de creek.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Dey all ax me, en when I fuse dey say dey ain't gwyne to make me go anyhow.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Dey ain't no fun in bein' as pop'lus as what I is, Brer Fox.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: If you wanter go, des get in ahead er de hounds en go lickety-split down de big road." Brer Fox rolled his little eyes and licked his chops where he dribble at de mouth, and put out to de barbecue; and he ain't mo' den made his disappearance, fo' here comes Brer Wolf; and when he got de news, off he put; and he ain't mo''n got out o' sight, fo' here comes ole Brer Bear; and when he hear talk o' de bacon meat and de big pan o' gravy, He sot up on his behind legs and snorted; den off he put; and he ain't got out of hearing 'fo' Brer Coon come racking up, and when he got the news he put out.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: So dah dey was; and what you gwyne do about it?
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: It seems like dey all got in front er de dogs—er, de dogs got behind 'em—and Brer Rabbit sot by de creekside laughing and hitting at de snake-doctors.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Hee hee!
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: And dem poor creturs had to go clean past de barbecue—if dey was any barbecue, which I don't scasely s'pect dey was.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: Dat what made me say what I does.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.text: When you git an invite to de barbecue, you better find out when and whar it's at, and who's runnin' it.
sentences.speaker: A

sentences.speaker: A
